## 前置讲义摘要（你必须基于这些已建立的认知继续，不要重复，要承接）

### u1-l1 项目定位与架构地图：pegainfer-server 是什么

本讲为手册首篇，确立项目全景。PegaInfer 是纯 Rust + CUDA 的 LLM 推理引擎，对外提供 OpenAI 兼容的 /v1 API，无 PyTorch 与 Python 运行时；设计原则是「共享基础设施、每个模型拥有自己的执行」。请求自上而下穿过：pegainfer-server（约 300 行的纯分发二进制，只做模型检测、CLI 校验、启动引擎）→ frontend（协议、分词、引擎契约）→ 各模型线 crate（经 ModelLine trait 接入，自带调度器与 prefill/decode 执行）→ core/kernels 与 KV 基础设施。Cargo feature 矩阵决定二进制编入哪些模型线：default 仅含 qwen3，其余经 --features 拉入。代码侧 model_lines() 是 cfg 守卫的注册向量，families() 是记录 model_type 与 compiled 状态的「第二真相源」，检测失败时由 feature_gate_hint 提示用 --features 重建；另指出 README 列 7 条线而代码有 8 个 feature（qwen4 为实验线未列入文档）。
### u1-l2 构建与运行：feature 矩阵、--release 与全局分配器

本讲以 Cargo.toml 与 main.rs 为源码落点，讲清同一份 main.rs 如何编出支持不同模型线的二进制。模块一：feature 矩阵——default 仅含 qwen3，各模型线经 optional 依赖按需拉入，gemma4、qwen35 等还要向 crate 内部同名 feature 转发以点亮内核面（qwen35 构建期需 Python+Triton）；main.rs 的 model_lines() 用 #[cfg] 守卫镜像 feature 表，未启用的线整体不参与编译，运行时 detect 也无法认领。模块二：二进制身份——包名 pegainfer-server、产物名 pegainfer 由 [[bin]] 决定，--version 输出来自 clap 字面量加编译期宏 CARGO_PKG_VERSION，根 workspace 的 default-members 使根目录 cargo run 直接可用。模块三：GPU 构建必须 --release——debug 档无优化且开调试断言，主机调度循环会拖垮 GPU 流水线；nvcc 侧优化不受 cargo profile 控制。模块四：非 msvc 平台经两处成对的 cfg 门（target 依赖与 #[global_allocator] static）换用 jemalloc 全局分配器。验证工具：cargo tree -e features 与 cargo metadata。
### u1-l3 main.rs 全景：从 CLI 到 serve 的启动主流程

本讲剖析 pegainfer-server 的 main.rs 启动主流程，覆盖三个最小模块：model_lines() 注册向量、main() 服务装配校验链、引擎加载与 Ctrl-C 两段式。核心结论：main() 是一条十余阶段的装配线——ModelLineRegistry 建表、clap 解析 CLI、读 config.json、detect 唯一认领模型线、三级校验（validate_provided 的 consume-or-reject、shared.validate 共享规则、line.validate 线内矩阵）、serve_plan 产出计划；廉价校验全部排在昂贵的引擎加载之前，且各阶段失败形态各异（clap 退出码 2、thiserror 模板、anyhow 上下文链、注册表启动 panic）。引擎加载放 spawn_blocking 与 HTTP 前端并行，前端在引擎注册后才 bind 端口以保持就绪语义；LoRA 分支因构建期需要控制平面而串行，且要求 LaunchedEngine::Stepped；Ctrl-C 在加载期保持默认 kill，引擎就绪后才挂优雅关停；tracing::flush 置于错误传播之前。引入的关键术语：trait 对象 ModelLine、provided_args、ServePlan、LaunchContext、LaunchedEngine 两代形态（Handle/Stepped），供后续单元承接。
### u1-l4 检测门：config.json 判定与 feature 提示

本讲拆解 server 启动流程中的「检测门」：在引擎加载之前裁决 config.json 归属哪条编译进来的模型线。registry.detect 有三种结果：唯一认领放行；Conflict（两条线抢同一配置）立即报错并点名双方，属注册表 bug；NoMatch 则收集每条编译线的拒绝原因后整体报错。各线的 probe 只做身份检查（model_type 与 architectures），契约是「恰好一条线认领」，尺寸校验留给后续阶段。因被编译掉的线连 probe 都不在二进制里，server 只能硬编码 families() 身份表，即「必要的第二真相源」，其 compiled 字段由 cfg! 编译期求值。feature_gate_hint 仅在 NoMatch 时被接线，查顶层与 text_config 中的 model_type 两个键，命中未编译家族即把 --features 重建建议拼在错误之后，且提示是 identity-only，不承诺 checkpoint 可服务。集成测试 detect_gate.rs 用冻结真 config 与最小 tokenizer 驱动真实二进制，互斥 cfg 的两个用例分别锁住 stock 构建的提示路径与 enabled 构建的「认领后 launch 诚实拒绝」路径，全程不触达 CUDA。
### u2-l1 ModelLine trait：server 与模型 crate 之间的接缝

本讲精读 pegainfer-frontend 的 model_line 模块，确立 server 与模型 crate 之间的接缝。核心结论：server 只持有一列 `&'static dyn ModelLine`，从不 import 模型 crate 的选项类型；接入新线＝实现 trait＋注册一行＋一个 Cargo feature。trait 共 8 个方法：name、probe、launch 必选，augment_cli、consumed_shared_args、arg_requirements、validate、serve_plan 均有默认实现；分工上 probe 做身份认领、validate 做廉价 CLI 规则、launch 才加载引擎。LaunchContext 为后三者提供只读世界（model_path、被认领的同一份 config、shared、合并命令的 matches），各线经 FromArgMatches 以 cli(ctx) 模式取回 crate 私有 CLI，类型知识不越过接缝。launch 返回 anyhow 的 LaunchedEngine（迁移期 legacy Handle／新 Stepped 二选一），调用方只加上下文传播不分支；错误语言是 DetectError（Conflict／NoMatch，server 仅对 NoMatch 附加 feature 重建提示）与 CliError（UnconsumedFlag／Rule），thiserror 模板即 API，测试逐字断言。Qwen3Line 是 8 方法满配参照，EchoLine 是三方法最小实现。
### u2-l2 SharedArgs：跨模型线共享的参数面

本讲义拆解 PegaInfer server 跨模型线共享的参数面（pegainfer-frontend 的 model_line.rs）。提出三层 flag 体系：核心 flag（CORE_ARGS，4 个，server 自消费、全线放行）、共享 flag（SharedArgs 其余 16 个，定义一次、消费权由各线 consumed_shared_args 声明）、线独占 flag（经 augment_cli 挂上）——「定义」与「使用权」分离是其核心设计。关键结论是一条共享 flag 要过四道门：值门（value_parser）与依赖门（requires_all，源自 SHARED_ARG_REQUIREMENTS 与各线 arg_requirements）在解析期由 clap 执行、尚未读 config.json；归属门（validate_provided 的 consume-or-reject）与语义门（SharedArgs::validate 加线内 validate）在模型检测后、引擎加载之前。两层规则分工判据：存在性依赖进依赖表，值/模式敏感规则手写进 validate。provided_args 借 clap 的 ValueSource 区分「用户显式提供」与「默认值填充」，该集合是各层校验的共同入参——值相同出身可不同，故只能按出身过滤而非比较值。u2-l3（注册表自检）与 u2-l4（Qwen3 校验矩阵）承接本讲。
### u2-l3 ModelLineRegistry：注册表与 CLI 归属自检

本讲聚焦 pegainfer-frontend 的 model_line.rs：ModelLineRegistry 与其查账员 RegistryClaims。因 clap 的 schema 断言在 release 构建中被禁用，注册表用「id 账＋拼写账」两本账（键映射到 ArgOwner：Shared 或某条线）在构造期以 panic 查出全部 flag 冲突；new 的流水线是共享 flag 先入账、核对 CORE_ARGS、逐线登记（线名唯一、consumed_shared_args 须指向真实共享 id）、依赖表收齐后统一校验，probe command 只承载单线独占 flag 供入账。detect 裁决配置归属：恰好一线认领，双认领即 DetectError::Conflict（注册表缺陷，立即返回），无人认领则 NoMatch 并逐线拼 rejections。validate_provided 执行 consume-or-reject：每个显式 flag（按 provided_args 的出身语义）须属核心、被消费共享或线独占之一，否则 CliError::UnconsumedFlag，错误文本即 API。parse_for_line 是单线注册表测试帮手，别线独占 flag 在其中报 unexpected argument 而非 UnconsumedFlag。分工原则：构造期 panic 管代码错，运行期 Err 管命令错。
### u2-l4 一条真实模型线：Qwen3Line 的独占 CLI 与校验矩阵

本讲把前三讲的抽象骨架落到默认编译进二进制的 Qwen3Line 上，覆盖三个模块：Qwen3Cli 独占 CLI、validate 冲突矩阵、launch 选项折叠。核心结论：十三个独占 flag 分五组（LoRA 服务、KV P2P/PD、显存预算、batch-invariant、EAGLE-3），类型私有、拼写公开，取值解析器在读取 config.json 之前就拦截格式错误；validate 用 provided 出身集合交叉共享与独占两面的当前值判定跨 flag 语义冲突，违反即返回 CliError::rule，全部发生在引擎加载之前；launch 把 SharedArgs 与 Qwen3Cli 折叠成 Qwen3LaunchOptions 交给 crate::launch，返回 LaunchedEngine::Stepped，启动策略归模型 crate 所有。引入的关键术语：provided 出身语义、consumed_shared_args 消费面、arg_requirements 依赖边、P/D 分离、投机解码、batch-invariant、三层分层失败——Loading engine 横幅是校验期与加载期的可观察分界线。
### u2-l5 ServePlan：引擎加载前就必须知道的服务形态

本讲讲解 ModelLine 的 serve_plan：因 HTTP 前端装配与分钟级引擎加载并行，模型线只能凭 CLI 与 config.json 在加载前产出 ServePlan 四字段——分区数 scheduler_partition_count（逻辑 DP rank）、prefill_only（P/D 分离的 prefill 角色）、lora_modules、auto_tool_call_parser。main() 依此三分支：LoRA 命中则串行等引擎、engine_count 硬编码 1；prefill-only 与默认分支把分区数作 engine_count 传给 serve 函数族。工具解析器经 resolve_tool_call_parser 按「显式选择 > 线自带默认 > Auto」折算，防上游按模型路径子串错配。前端先按 engine_count（TransportMode::Bootstrapped）注册 engine identity，引擎就绪后与实际分区数对账，不符即取消服务——分区数是请求寻址参数，宁可死不带病服务；各线应以 ..ServePlan::default() 展开实现以防漂移。
### u3-l1 引擎契约总览：两代契约并存的地图

本讲给出 pegainfer-frontend 引擎契约的总地图。engine 模块按内聚性拆成 13 个子模块，mod.rs 以 pub use 扁平 re-export，使 engine::X 外部路径不随分拆改变。契约分两代并存：新一代 step 驱动契约（step/ledger/request_lifecycle/metrics/wiring/driver/control）与迁移中的 legacy 每 token 契约（request/event/sink/kv/handle），stop 是不入组的共享词汇。核心类型 LaunchedEngine 是迁移期二选一枚举：Handle 变体装 legacy EngineHandle，Stepped 变体装 step 交接包 Engine（含 schedulers、EngineInfo、lora，Option 即能力），全部模型线迁完后该枚举将删除。普查结论：qwen3/qwen35/gemma4/k3 已返回 Stepped，deepseek-v2-lite/glm52/kimi-k2 仍为 Handle，qwen4 直接报错；LoRA 分支只认 Stepped。生产者是模型 crate 侧调度器，消费者是 frontend 协议栈。
### u3-l2 legacy 契约线类型：GenerateRequest、TokenEvent 与 TokenSink

本讲覆盖 legacy 契约的三个线类型模块：GenerateRequest、TokenEvent 族与 TokenSink，辅读 SamplingParams 与 vllm 支构造点。核心结论：GenerateRequest 是纯数据请求本体，十二个字段不含引擎内部状态——data_parallel_rank 是路由指令（None 交 handle 选最低负载分区，桥恒绑 rank），token_tx 是唯一事件出口，trace_parent 携带可 Copy 的追踪上下文。TokenEvent 共七个变体，「Scheduled 先行、terminal（Finished/Error/Rejected）恰一次」在 legacy 侧只是约定而非类型保证；FinishReason（Length/Stop/Error）是被新契约复用的完结词汇；RequestTag=Arc<str> 使每事件打标只是一次引用计数。TokenSink 用一条共享打标通道加单一 demux 循环取代每请求通道，每步唤醒数由 N 降至约 1；取消从 drop 接收端改为每请求的原子 abort reason（None/Cancelled/Disconnected，Release 写 Acquire 读），tx.is_closed() 是引擎级信号，abort 才是每请求信号。这些类型仍服务于 deepseek-v2-lite、glm52、kimi-k2 三条未迁移模型线，也是 u4 引擎桥 demux 事件流的前提。
### u3-l3 step 契约线类型：StepOutputs 与扁平 RequestUpdate

本讲精读 step 契约的线类型，覆盖 step.rs 与 stop.rs 两个模块。核心结论是「顺序即结构」：一个调度器步产出一条 StepOutputs，每个被触碰请求至多一条扁平 RequestUpdate；旧 TokenEvent 协议靠文档约定的「先调度、终态恰一次」时序被编码成字段的物理排列，终态之后再出 token 在类型上不可表达，跨步保证由账本承接（触碰已关账户即 panic）。关键术语：RequestId 是进程内路由的整数 newtype，由提交点铸造，外部字符串 id 留在协议栈；Request 是纯负载，history_tokens 与 history_marks（新者在前）是多轮会话前缀快照的恢复点坐标；Terminal 三态（完结/拒绝/失败）且拒绝原因类型化；StopPolicy 归一化停止集合、以 EOS 优先判定，StopCause 随终态上行且触发 token 保留。消费侧按「接纳事实→新 token→终态」的字段顺序折叠。
### u3-l4 RequestLedger：活请求的账本与 terminal 恰一次

本讲精读 pegainfer-frontend 的 RequestLedger：它为每个未答复请求开「账户」，账户不存负载（submit 时已所有权转移给调度器），只记引擎欠客户端的事实——abort 标志引用、prompt 长度、排队时间与 token 流水。生命周期单向：register 开户（Queued）→ admit 转 Active → 流式记账 → finish/fail/reject/retire/defer_finish 五种关户，账本 Drop 再把残留账户销账为 Failed，与信封、DeferredFinish 的 drop 炸弹合成「应答到底」三层保护。核心结论「terminal 恰一次」由所有权移除强制：关户即从 HashMap 移走账户，触碰已关或未知账户在出错调用点 panic 且 release 构建仍生效；终态计数只出自账本流水，模型侧算术插不进来。register/commit_step/fail_all 为 pub(crate)，节奏归 driver；StepStatement 把同一步的多次记账合并为每请求至多一条更新。
### u3-l5 Scheduler trait 与 drive 轮询循环

本讲精读 pegainfer-frontend 的 driver.rs，模块仅此一处轮询循环。核心结论：`Scheduler` trait 把模型线的全部运行时义务压缩为三方法——`submit` 只做所有权转移（裁决延迟到 step 零代价）、`step` 是唯一裁决点与唯一记账点、`metrics` 为只读快照；超出三方法的能力（如 LoRA 控制）由调度器自建通道、在自己的 step 里排空。`drive` 循环把八条模型线的循环纪律固化为代码：每迭代排空提交（先 register 开户再 submit）、step、发布 metrics、commit_step 恰好一次，保证一步至多一条 StepOutputs；metrics 变化用空更新的「唤醒消息」信号。致命路径 fail_all 以错误原文写销全部在途请求；优雅退出要求通道断开且账本排空，空转 spin_loop 绝不睡眠。spawn_scheduler 经 scheduler_pair 铸 SchedulerHandle/SchedulerBackend 双端并起命名线程，交回 LiveScheduler。关键术语（三方法、drive 四拍、commit_step/fail_all、唤醒消息、排空退出）为下一讲 scheduler_pair 接线与多分区路由铺垫。
### u3-l6 接线与路由：scheduler_pair、Engine 与 legacy EngineHandle

本讲精读 wiring.rs、handle.rs 与 kv.rs，讲清引擎契约的接线与路由。核心结论：scheduler_pair「铸造而非组装」双端——提交走 crossbeam（同步消费者在调度器线程）、步流走 tokio mpsc（异步消费者在协议栈）、metrics 用 Arc<Mutex> 共享单元只存最新值并以步流空消息唤醒；submit 永不失败，调度器死后由信封 drop 炸弹以 Failed terminal 作答。Engine/EngineInfo 是协议栈溶解的交接包，kv_capacity 与 servable_len 的 None 各有显式语义（跳过 batch-fit 检查／不钳制最大长度）；LaunchedEngine 是迁移期 Handle/Stepped 二选一枚举。legacy EngineHandle 的路由决策树：已解析 KvPrefix 的 rank 压倒调用方绑定（hold 把块钉在该 rank 上，不一致即调用方 bug），否则取 running+4×waiting 最低分分区（并列取小下标），越界 rank 以 Scheduled→Rejected 事件应答并返回 Ok。关键术语：信封 drop 炸弹、take_steps 只发一次、metrics watches 兼任 DP 拓扑声明、路由范围（submit_txs 数）与拓扑声明（watches 数）两个真相。
### u4-l1 serve 函数族：并发加载与装配骨架

# 项目学习手册·单篇讲义生成 Worker

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

---

## 代码实践要求

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

实践优先从以下位置寻找依据：

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。
- 根据测试断言理解行为。
- 修改局部参数并说明应该观察什么。
- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

405	#[derive(Default)]
406	struct RegistryClaims {
407	    ids: BTreeMap<String, ArgOwner>,
408	    spellings: BTreeMap<String, ArgOwner>,
409	}
410	
411	impl RegistryClaims {
412	    fn register_command(&mut self, command: &clap::Command, owner: ArgOwner) -> BTreeSet<String> {
413	        command
414	            .get_arguments()
415	            .map(|arg| self.register_arg(arg, owner))
416	            .collect()
417	    }
418	
419	    fn register_arg(&mut self, arg: &clap::Arg, owner: ArgOwner) -> String {
420	        let id = arg.get_id().to_string();
421	        self.claim_id(id.clone(), owner);
422	        for long in arg
423	            .get_long()
424	            .into_iter()
425	            .chain(arg.get_all_aliases().into_iter().flatten())
426	        {
427	            self.claim_spelling(format!("--{long}"), owner);
428	        }
429	        for short in arg
430	            .get_short()
431	            .into_iter()
432	            .chain(arg.get_all_short_aliases().into_iter().flatten())
433	        {
434	            self.claim_spelling(format!("-{short}"), owner);
435	        }
436	        id
437	    }
438	
439	    fn claim_id(&mut self, id: String, owner: ArgOwner) {
440	        if let Some(previous) = self.ids.get(&id) {
441	            if *previous == ArgOwner::Shared {
442	                if let ArgOwner::Line(name) = owner {
443	                    panic!(
444	                        "model line {name} redeclares SharedArgs flag id {id:?}; list it in consumed_shared_args instead"
445	                    );
446	                }
447	            }
448	            panic!("{previous} and {owner} both define flag id {id:?}");
449	        }
450	        self.ids.insert(id, owner);
451	    }
452	
453	    fn claim_spelling(&mut self, spelling: String, owner: ArgOwner) {
454	        if let Some(previous) = self.spellings.get(&spelling) {
455	            panic!("{previous} and {owner} both define CLI spelling {spelling:?}");
456	        }
457	        self.spellings.insert(spelling, owner);
458	    }
459	
460	    fn is_shared_id(&self, id: &str) -> bool {
461	        self.ids.get(id) == Some(&ArgOwner::Shared)
462	    }
463	
464	    fn validate_requirement(&self, owner: ArgOwner, source: &str, targets: &[&str]) {
465	        assert!(
466	            self.ids.get(source) == Some(&owner),
467	            "{owner} declares requirements for unowned flag id {source:?}"
468	        );
469	        for &target in targets {
470	            assert!(source != target, "flag id {source:?} cannot require itself");
471	            let target_owner = self.ids.get(target);
472	            assert!(
473	                target_owner == Some(&ArgOwner::Shared) || target_owner == Some(&owner),
474	                "{owner} flag id {source:?} requires unknown or foreign argument id {target:?}"
475	            );
476	        }
477	    }
478	}
479	
480	fn register_line(
481	    line: &'static dyn ModelLine,
482	    owner: ArgOwner,
483	    claims: &mut RegistryClaims,
484	) -> LineEntry {
485	    for id in line.consumed_shared_args() {
486	        assert!(
487	            claims.is_shared_id(id),
488	            "model line {} consumes unknown SharedArgs flag id {id:?}",
489	            line.name()
490	        );
491	    }
492	    let command = line.augment_cli(clap::Command::new("probe"));
493	    let own_ids = claims.register_command(&command, owner);
494	    LineEntry { line, own_ids }
495	}

497	/// The server binary's fixed list of compiled-in model lines.
498	pub struct ModelLineRegistry {
499	    entries: Vec<LineEntry>,
500	    requirements: BTreeMap<&'static str, &'static [&'static str]>,
501	}
502	
503	impl ModelLineRegistry {
504	    /// Validates CLI ownership explicitly because Clap's equivalent schema
505	    /// assertions are disabled in release builds.
506	    pub fn new(lines: Vec<&'static dyn ModelLine>) -> Self {
507	        let shared_cmd = SharedArgs::augment_args(clap::Command::new("probe"));
508	        let mut claims = RegistryClaims::default();
509	        claims.register_command(&shared_cmd, ArgOwner::Shared);
510	        for id in CORE_ARGS {
511	            assert!(
512	                claims.is_shared_id(id),
513	                "CORE_ARGS contains unknown SharedArgs flag id {id:?}"
514	            );
515	        }
516	        let mut pending_requirements = SHARED_ARG_REQUIREMENTS
517	            .iter()
518	            .map(|&(source, targets)| (ArgOwner::Shared, source, targets))
519	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
520	        let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(lines.len());
521	        let mut line_names = BTreeSet::new();
522	        for line in lines {
523	            let name = line.name();
524	            assert!(
525	                line_names.insert(name),
526	                "duplicate model line name {name:?}"
527	            );
528	            let owner = ArgOwner::Line(name);
529	            entries.push(register_line(line, owner, &mut claims));
530	            pending_requirements.extend(
531	                line.arg_requirements()
532	                    .iter()
533	                    .map(|&(source, targets)| (owner, source, targets)),
534	            );
535	        }
536	        let mut requirements = BTreeMap::new();
537	        for (owner, source, targets) in pending_requirements {
538	            claims.validate_requirement(owner, source, targets);
539	            assert!(
540	                requirements.insert(source, targets).is_none(),
541	                "{owner} declares requirements more than once for flag id {source:?}"
542	            );
543	        }
544	        Self {
545	            entries,
546	            requirements,
547	        }
548	    }
549	
550	    /// The full server command: shared flags plus every line's exclusive
551	    /// flags, so `--help` and parsing don't depend on the detected model.
552	    pub fn build_command(&self, cmd: clap::Command) -> clap::Command {
553	        let mut cmd = SharedArgs::augment_args(cmd);
554	        for entry in &self.entries {
555	            cmd = entry.line.augment_cli(cmd);
556	        }
557	        // `mut_arg` re-appends each source and would reorder `--help`.
558	        cmd.mut_args(|arg| {
559	            let Some(targets) = self.requirements.get(arg.get_id().as_str()) else {
560	                return arg;
561	            };
562	            arg.requires_all(targets.iter().copied())
563	        })
564	    }

566	    /// Find the unique line that claims this `config.json`. On
567	    /// [`DetectError::NoMatch`] the caller may prepend a hint for families
568	    /// that exist but were compiled out.
569	    pub fn detect(
570	        &self,
571	        config: &serde_json::Value,
572	    ) -> Result<&'static dyn ModelLine, DetectError> {
573	        let mut rejections = Vec::new();
574	        let mut claimed: Option<&'static dyn ModelLine> = None;
575	        for entry in &self.entries {
576	            match entry.line.probe(config) {
577	                Ok(()) => match claimed {
578	                    None => claimed = Some(entry.line),
579	                    Some(prev) => {
580	                        return Err(DetectError::Conflict {
581	                            first: prev.name(),
582	                            second: entry.line.name(),
583	                        });
584	                    }
585	                },
586	                Err(reason) => rejections.push(format!("{}: {reason}", entry.line.name())),
587	            }
588	        }
589	        claimed.ok_or_else(|| {
590	            let render = |key: &str| {
591	                config
592	                    .get(key)
593	                    .map_or_else(|| "missing".to_string(), std::string::ToString::to_string)
594	            };
595	            DetectError::NoMatch {
596	                model_type: render("model_type"),
597	                architectures: render("architectures"),
598	                rejections,
599	            }
600	        })
601	    }
602	
603	    /// Consume-or-reject: every explicitly provided flag must be a core flag,
604	    /// a shared flag the detected line consumes, or one of the line's own.
605	    pub fn validate_provided(
606	        &self,
607	        detected: &'static dyn ModelLine,
608	        provided: &BTreeSet<String>,
609	        cmd: &clap::Command,
610	    ) -> Result<(), CliError> {
611	        let entry = self
612	            .entries
613	            .iter()
614	            .find(|entry| std::ptr::eq(entry.line, detected))
615	            .expect("detected line came from this registry");
616	        for id in provided {
617	            let id = id.as_str();
618	            if CORE_ARGS.contains(&id)
619	                || detected.consumed_shared_args().contains(&id)
620	                || entry.own_ids.contains(id)
621	            {
622	                continue;
623	            }
624	            return Err(CliError::UnconsumedFlag {
625	                flag: long_flag(cmd, id),
626	                line: detected.name(),
627	            });
628	        }
629	        Ok(())
630	    }
631	}

633	fn long_flag(cmd: &clap::Command, id: &str) -> String {
634	    cmd.get_arguments()
635	        .find(|arg| arg.get_id() == id)
636	        .and_then(clap::Arg::get_long)
637	        .map_or_else(|| id.to_owned(), str::to_owned)
638	}

640	/// Arg ids the user set explicitly (command line or env), for consume-or-reject.
641	pub fn provided_args(matches: &clap::ArgMatches, cmd: &clap::Command) -> BTreeSet<String> {
642	    // matches.ids() also yields clap's synthetic group ids; keep only real args.
643	    let real: BTreeSet<&str> = cmd
644	        .get_arguments()
645	        .map(|arg| arg.get_id().as_str())
646	        .collect();
647	    matches
648	        .ids()
649	        .map(clap::Id::as_str)
650	        .filter(|id| real.contains(id))
651	        .filter(|id| {
652	            matches!(
653	                matches.value_source(id),
654	                Some(
655	                    clap::parser::ValueSource::CommandLine | clap::parser::ValueSource::EnvVariable
656	                )
657	            )
658	        })
659	        .map(str::to_owned)
660	        .collect()
661	}

665	/// Test helper: parse `argv` against shared flags plus one line's flags, the
666	/// way the server binary does for a detected line. Exposed for model-crate
667	/// unit tests; not a serving entry point.
668	pub fn parse_for_line(
669	    line: &'static dyn ModelLine,
670	    argv: &[&str],
671	) -> anyhow::Result<(SharedArgs, clap::ArgMatches, BTreeSet<String>)> {
672	    use clap::FromArgMatches;
673	    let registry = ModelLineRegistry::new(vec![line]);
674	    let cmd = registry.build_command(clap::Command::new("pegainfer"));
675	    let matches = cmd.clone().try_get_matches_from(argv)?;
676	    let shared = SharedArgs::from_arg_matches(&matches)?;
677	    let provided = provided_args(&matches, &cmd);
678	    registry.validate_provided(line, &provided, &cmd)?;
679	    shared.validate(&provided)?;
680	    Ok((shared, matches, provided))
681	}

30 31 PegaInfer serves LLMs through an OpenAI-compatible API. Each model owns its scheduler, state, and kernels; serving and KV infrastructure are shared. No PyTorch or Python runtime. 32 33 ## Quickstart 34 35 ### Prebuilt binary · Qwen3 on Linux 36 37 The Qwen3-only release bundles CUDA 13 and cuBLAS. It requires **Linux x86_64**, an NVIDIA GPU with compute capability **8.x–12.x**, driver **580+**, glibc **2.35+**, and OpenSSL **3**. Model weights are downloaded separately. 38 39 ```bash 40 curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pegainfer-project/pegainfer/main/install.sh | bash 41 ``` 42 43 Download [Qwen3-4B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-4B) into `models/Qwen3-4B`, then start the server: 44 45 ```bash 46 pegainfer --model-path models/Qwen3-4B 47 ``` 48 49 The server listens on port **8000**. If the command is not on your shell's path: 50 51 ```bash 52 export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" 53 ``` 54 55 The installer selects the latest release by default. `PEGAINFER_VERSION` selects an exact version; see [releases](https://github.com/pegainfer-project/pegainfer/releases). 56 57 ### Build from source 58 59 Use the Rust toolchain pinned in [rust-toolchain.toml](rust-toolchain.toml), a CUDA Toolkit with `nvcc` and cuBLAS, and a compatible NVIDIA driver. The default Qwen3 build needs no Python. Its driver floor is R545 / CUDA 12.3; newer toolkits and model-specific kernels can require a newer driver. 60 61 From the repository root, with the checkpoint downloaded: 62 63 ```bash 64 export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda 65 cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B 66 ``` 67 68 Always use **`--release`** for GPU builds. The server entrypoint is `pegainfer-server`; model crates contain the model implementation and diagnostics. 69 70

1	# Frontend architecture: pegainfer-frontend and the engine boundary
2	
3	**TL;DR:** `pegainfer-frontend` owns everything north of the model schedulers: the engine contract, the vLLM protocol stack, and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. The contract now has two generations living side by side: the **step contract** (`StepOutputs` wire + `RequestLedger` lifecycle + a contract-owned polling driver — Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Gemma 4 and `pegainfer-sim` are migrated) and the **legacy handle contract** (`EngineHandle` + `TokenEvent` per-request events — glm52/kimi-k2/deepseek-v2-lite still launch through it). The vLLM Rust dependency revision is recorded in `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`. **Next step: migrate glm52, then delete the legacy contract.**
4	
5	Last touched: 2026-10
6	
7	## The boundary, in one sentence
8	
9	An engine is a set of schedulers, each a `Scheduler` implementation driven by the contract's polling loop: *the frontend submits `Request`s into a scheduler and receives a `StepOutputs` message for each step with request updates or metric changes, with each request's updates merged into one flat `RequestUpdate`; requests finish, fail or are rejected with one terminal, while cancellation retires them silently.* Tokenizer, chat templates, HTTP, metrics, LoRA routing live north of the scheduler; KV, batching, CUDA live south. How many schedulers an engine exposes and what each one means (DP rank, P/D role) is the model line's decision; the contract attaches no rank semantics, and TP/EP lockstep is encapsulated below the `Scheduler` impl. Placement across schedulers is frontend policy over the load feed.
10	
11	## The step contract
12	
13	```
14	pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/
15	├── step.rs              # the wire: RequestId, Request, QueuedRequest,
16	│                        #   StepOutputs { Vec<RequestUpdate> },
17	│                        #   RequestUpdate { scheduled, tokens, logprobs, cached_tokens,
18	│                        #   prompt_echo, kv_transfer, terminal }, Terminal
19	├── request_lifecycle.rs # submission envelope, abort control and step sender plumbing;
20	│                        #   DeferredFinish remains available for P/D handoff
21	├── ledger.rs            # RequestLedger: admit/reject/push/finish/fail/retire,
22	│                        #   prompt/completion tallies, one merged update per touched id
23	├── wiring.rs            # scheduler_pair, SchedulerHandle (submit/take_steps/metrics),
24	│                        #   Engine { schedulers, info, lora }, LiveScheduler,
25	│                        #   EngineInfo, LaunchedEngine { Handle | Stepped }
26	├── control.rs           # LoRA capability — outside the contract: LoraControl vocabulary,
27	│                        #   LoraClient (the `Engine.lora: Option<LoraClient>` capability)
28	└── driver.rs            # trait Scheduler { submit, step, metrics } + spawn_scheduler:
29	                         #   the contract-owned pure-polling drive loop
30	```
31	
32	Design decisions worth knowing before touching it:
33	
34	- **Step-batched wire.** One message per scheduler step with request updates or metric changes, not one channel per request: the scheduler's natural output unit is the step batch, and per-request channels were tried and rejected (the scheduler for-loop over N channels was the bottleneck). The protocol stack demuxes.
35	- **Flat `RequestUpdate`.** All facts a step produced for one request travel in one struct, so intra-request ordering is structure, not convention. The ledger merges every write for an id into that one record before the driver commits the step.
36	- **Typed stop contract.** `Request.stop_policy` keeps model EOS handling separate from explicit request stop IDs. A token-driven finish retains the triggering token in the emitted output and carries `Terminal::Finished.stop_cause`: The vLLM primary EOS maps to `Eos(id)` with no wire `stop_reason`; secondary EOS IDs join the explicit stop set and map to `Token(id)`, reporting the actual matching ID. `ignore_eos` disables only model EOS.
37	- **Ledger lifecycle.** `RequestLedger` owns one account for every unanswered submission. A scheduler receives only `QueuedRequest { id, request }` and writes every lifecycle transition by id. The ledger rejects touches after closure, derives completion counts from `push_tokens`, and writes off every open account when an engine-fatal `step` error ends the driver.
38	- **Ledger as single writer.** Schedulers never touch the step channel; they call ledger methods. `admit` stamps `ScheduledInfo` from the registered prompt length, `push_tokens` tallies completions, and `commit_step` publishes the merged statement once per driver iteration.
39	- **Polling driver, scheduler-owned park.** `spawn_scheduler` owns the serve loop: drain submissions, `Scheduler::step`, publish metrics, commit. An idle iteration ends in a `spin_loop` hint. Gemma 4 has one deliberate park inside this policy: while async prefill is the only remaining work, its scheduler drains the lane and joins it rather than hot-polling the completion (a drain failure is engine-fatal); when decode or queued work exists it keeps polling the lane without blocking. Qwen3.5 likewise polls its in-flight prefill while decode is active, but waits on the prefill event inside the step when no decoder remains.
40	- **Abort is a flag, not channel teardown.** `SchedulerHandle::submit` returns a `RequestControl`; the frontend flips its boolean abort flag and the scheduler retires the request silently on its next touch (no terminal — the frontend already dropped its state for that id).
41	- **Channels:** the submit channel is crossbeam (sync consumer on the scheduler thread), steps are tokio mpsc (async consumer in the bridge); load is a shared cell read via `SchedulerHandle::metrics()`. 42	- **Control plane lives outside the contract.** `Scheduler` has no control method and the contract carries no control channel. 43	- **A scheduler that exits stops the server.** Once the driver returns or its thread unwinds, `SchedulerHandle::exited` resolves and the stepped bridge fails after forwarding what is already on the step stream. 45	### Onboarding checklist for a new model line
46	
47	1. Implement `Scheduler` (see `Qwen3Scheduler` in `pegainfer-qwen3/src/frontend_adapter.rs` — the whole adaptation is deliberately in one file):
48	   - `submit(queued)` — ownership transfer only: park `QueuedRequest { id, request }`. No verdict here by design — `step` is the single ledger-writing site, and the driver commits once per iteration.
49	   - `step(ledger)` — one scheduling step: admit/reject, execute, push tokens, finish/fail/retire. Return `Err` only for engine-fatal states.
50	   - `metrics()` — KV occupancy + running/waiting counts for routers and shutdown draining.
51	   - Extra capabilities (LoRA etc.) are not trait methods: mint the private channel before spawning, close the scheduler over the receiver, drain it inside `step`.
52	2. `spawn_scheduler(name, scheduler)` per scheduler, or `scheduler_pair` plus `drive` when launch must await thread-local initialization, as single-GPU Qwen3.5 does for CUDA/cuBLAS; return `Engine { schedulers, info: EngineInfo { kv_capacity, servable_len }, lora }` — the required-metadata fields are the checklist, and `lora: Some(client)` only when the line actually serves adapter control.

54	
55	The contract's own invariants are tested in `ledger.rs`/`driver.rs` tests; the qwen3 adapter's contract tests (`frontend_adapter/tests.rs`) are the CPU reference for testing a model's protocol behaviour end to end with a fake executor. 56	
57	## The legacy handle contract (migration pending)
58	
59	`request.rs`/`event.rs`/`sink.rs`/`kv.rs`/`handle.rs` still carry the previous generation: `launch -> EngineHandle`, per-request `TokenSink` events (`Scheduled … Token* … terminal` by convention), send-failure-as-cancellation. glm52, kimi-k2 and deepseek-v2-lite launch through it (`LaunchedEngine::Handle`), and the vllm stack keeps both bridge paths (`bridge.rs` for handles, `bridge/stepped.rs` for step engines). 60	
61	## Crate layout
62	
63	```
64	pegainfer-frontend
65	├── engine/            # both contract generations, re-exported flat
66	├── sampler.rs         # SamplingParams
67	├── parallel.rs        # ParallelConfig
68	├── tracing_state.rs   # global tracing on/off flag (frontend + schedulers both read it)
69	├── model_line.rs      # ModelLine trait + ModelLineRegistry + SharedArgs (dispatch seam)
70	└── vllm/              # protocol stack #1: vLLM EngineCore impersonation over ZMQ
71	    ├── mod.rs         #   serve_* entry points; engine_task fans out per LaunchedEngine arm
72	    ├── bridge.rs      #   LocalEngineBridge (legacy handle path) + shared BridgeLink
73	    ├── bridge/stepped.rs  # SteppedEngineBridge: StepOutputs -> EngineCore messages
74	    ├── wire.rs        #   EngineCoreSamplingParams <-> SamplingParams translation
75	    ├── lora.rs        #   /v1/{load,unload}_lora_adapter over LoraClient
76	    ├── reasoning_effort.rs  # chat-route reasoning_effort -> the template's vocabulary
77	    ├── history.rs     #   chat-route history boundary -> vllm_xargs.generation_prompt_tokens -> Request::history_tokens
78	    └── request_contract.rs  # GLM5.2 prefill-only route guard
79	```
80

82	
83	## ModelLine: what a new model provides
84	
85	`model_line.rs` defines the dispatch seam. A model crate implements `ModelLine` (each crate has a `model_line.rs` exporting `pub static MODEL_LINE`):
86	
87	- `name()` — family name for logs and errors.
88	- `probe(config_json) -> Result<(), String>` — claim or reject the model directory by its identity fields; exactly one registered line must claim a config.

94	All six lines are onboarded. Adding a model line = write `model_line.rs` in the crate + one registry entry + one Cargo feature.

97	
98	**`vllm` (current default, fleet-proven).** Impersonates a vLLM EngineCore process over in-process ZMQ/msgpack because upstream `vllm-server` assumes the engine is a separate process. 1	# Frontend architecture: pegainfer-frontend and the engine boundary
2	
3	**TL;DR:** `pegainfer-frontend` owns everything north of the model schedulers: the engine contract, the vLLM protocol stack, and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. The contract now has two generations living side by side: the **step contract** (`StepOutputs` wire + `RequestLedger` lifecycle + a contract-owned polling driver — Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Gemma 4 and `pegainfer-sim` are migrated) and the **legacy handle contract** (`EngineHandle` + `TokenEvent` per-request events — glm52/kimi-k2/deepseek-v2-lite still launch through it). The vLLM Rust dependency revision is recorded in `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`. **Next step: migrate glm52, then delete the legacy contract.**
4	
5	Last touched: 2026-10
6	
7	## The boundary, in one sentence
8	
9	An engine is a set of schedulers, each a `Scheduler` implementation driven by the contract's polling loop: *the frontend submits `Request`s into a scheduler and receives a `StepOutputs` message for each step with request updates or metric changes, with each request's updates merged into one flat `RequestUpdate`; requests finish, fail or are rejected with one terminal, while cancellation retires them silently.* Tokenizer, chat templates, HTTP, metrics, LoRA routing live north of the scheduler; KV, batching, CUDA live south. The contract contains no CUDA types, and the frontend holds no model-layer structs — everything it touches is a contract type (channels, `JoinHandle<()>`, POD info). How many schedulers an engine exposes and what each one means (DP rank, P/D role) is the model line's decision; the contract attaches no rank semantics, and TP/EP lockstep is encapsulated below the `Scheduler` impl. Placement across schedulers is frontend policy over the load feed.
10	
11	## The step contract
12	
13	```
14	pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/
15	├── step.rs              # the wire: RequestId, Request, QueuedRequest,
16	│                        #   StepOutputs { Vec<RequestUpdate> },
17	│                        #   RequestUpdate { scheduled, tokens, logprobs, cached_tokens,
18	│                        #   prompt_echo, kv_transfer, terminal }, Terminal
19	├── request_lifecycle.rs # submission envelope, abort control and step sender plumbing;
20	│                        #   DeferredFinish remains available for P/D handoff
21	├── ledger.rs            # RequestLedger: admit/reject/push/finish/fail/retire,
22	│                        #   prompt/completion tallies, one merged update per touched id
23	├── wiring.rs            # scheduler_pair, SchedulerHandle (submit/take_steps/metrics),
24	│                        #   Engine { schedulers, info, lora }, LiveScheduler,
25	│                        #   EngineInfo, LaunchedEngine { Handle | Stepped }
26	├── control.rs           # LoRA capability — outside the contract: LoraControl vocabulary,
27	│                        #   LoraClient (the `Engine.lora: Option<LoraClient>` capability)
28	└── driver.rs            # trait Scheduler { submit, step, metrics } + spawn_scheduler:
29	                         #   the contract-owned pure-polling drive loop
30	```
31	
32	Design decisions worth knowing before touching it:
33	
34	- **Step-batched wire.** One message per scheduler step with request updates or metric changes, not one channel per request: the scheduler's natural output unit is the step batch, and per-request channels were tried and rejected (the scheduler for-loop over N channels was the bottleneck). The protocol stack demuxes.
35	- **Flat `RequestUpdate`.** All facts a step produced for one request travel in one struct, so intra-request ordering is structure, not convention. The ledger merges every write for an id into that one record before the driver commits the step.
36	- **Typed stop contract.** `Request.stop_policy` keeps model EOS handling separate from explicit request stop IDs. A token-driven finish retains the triggering token in the emitted output and carries `Terminal::Finished.stop_cause`: The vLLM primary EOS maps to `Eos(id)` with no wire `stop_reason`; secondary EOS IDs join the explicit stop set and map to `Token(id)`, reporting the actual matching ID. `ignore_eos` disables only model EOS.
37	- **Ledger lifecycle.** `RequestLedger` owns one account for every unanswered submission. A scheduler receives only `QueuedRequest { id, request }` and writes every lifecycle transition by id. The ledger rejects touches after closure, derives completion counts from `push_tokens`, and writes off every open account when an engine-fatal `step` error ends the driver.
38	- **Ledger as single writer.** Schedulers never touch the step channel; they call ledger methods. `admit` stamps `ScheduledInfo` from the registered prompt length, `push_tokens` tallies completions, and `commit_step` publishes the merged statement once per driver iteration.
39	- **Polling driver, scheduler-owned park.** `spawn_scheduler` owns the serve loop: drain submissions, `Scheduler::step`, publish metrics, commit. An idle iteration ends in a `spin_loop` hint. Gemma 4 has one deliberate park inside this policy: while async prefill is the only remaining work, its scheduler drains the lane and joins it rather than hot-polling the completion (a drain failure is engine-fatal); when decode or queued work exists it keeps polling the lane without blocking. Qwen3.5 likewise polls its in-flight prefill while decode is active, but waits on the prefill event inside the step when no decoder remains.
40	- **Abort is a flag, not channel teardown.** `SchedulerHandle::submit` returns a `RequestControl`; the frontend flips its boolean abort flag and the scheduler retires the request silently on its next touch (no terminal — the frontend already dropped its state for that id).
41	- **Channels:** the submit channel is crossbeam (sync consumer on the scheduler thread), steps are tokio mpsc (async consumer in the bridge); load is a shared cell read via `SchedulerHandle::metrics()`. Metric changes without request updates send an empty step, so cancellation can reset HTTP gauges; unchanged polling iterations send nothing. All channels unbounded on purpose — admission control is the scheduler's job, expressed as `Rejected`, never as backpressure on submit.
42	- **Control plane lives outside the contract.** `Scheduler` has no control method and the contract carries no control channel. A capability like LoRA is a private channel the model crate mints *before* `spawn_scheduler` — the scheduler closes over the receiver, the `LoraClient` sender surfaces as `Engine.lora: Option<LoraClient>`, and the `Option` *is* the capability (no `bool` flag, no registry until a second capability exists). The vocabulary (`LoraControl`, `LoraClient`) is still defined in the frontend crate because the frontend must speak it without holding model structs; only the wiring is the model's business.
43	- **A scheduler that exits stops the server.** Once the driver returns or its thread unwinds, `SchedulerHandle::exited` resolves and the stepped bridge fails after forwarding what is already on the step stream. A failing stepped bridge gives its output sender up to a second to flush, ending with the `ENGINE_CORE_DEAD` sentinel, which makes the engine core client fail every request it still tracks, including ones no bridge has read. The server then shuts down so it can be restarted, and every other bridge aborts its requests and flushes its output before the scheduler threads are joined.

# u5-l2 · 从零接入一条新模型线：完整清单

## 1. 本讲目标

本讲是前四个单元的收官：把散落在 `ModelLine` trait（u2-l1）、注册表自检（u2-l3）、`Scheduler` 契约（u3-l5）、serve 函数族（u4-l1）里的知识，收拢成一份**可照着做的新模型线接入清单**。整份清单有官方参考实现——`pegainfer-frontend/examples/echo-server.rs`，一个不含 GPU、不含权重的完整模型线。

学完本讲，你应该能：

- 按顺序复述接入步骤：**实现 `ModelLine` → 注册进 `model_lines()` → Cargo feature → `families()` 行 + 单测 → detect_gate 式端到端测试**；
- 解释 echo-server.rs 为什么是官方参考：它把 probe + Scheduler + launch + 镜像 main 的服务流程全部装进一个无 GPU 的 example；
- 说出 detect_gate.rs 的双 fixture 设计——冻结 config 来自模型 crate（qwen4），tokenizer 来自 echo-model，两条断言路径都不触达 CUDA。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲假设你已读完 u2-l1（trait 接缝）、u2-l3（注册表两本账）、u3-l5（三方法调度器）与 u4-l1（serve 装配骨架）。在此之上补三个工程层面的概念：

- **example 即参考实现**：Cargo 的 `examples/` 目录通常放演示代码，但这个仓库把 echo-server.rs 当作「接入新线的活文档」维护——文件头注释明确写着 "It doubles as the reference for wiring a model line in"。它的价值在于：新线作者不需要读 8 个模型 crate 的差异，只需要读这 234 行的**最小完整实现**。
- **`CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name>` 环境变量**：cargo 为集成测试（`tests/` 目录）注入的编译期变量，值是本 crate 二进制的绝对路径。集成测试用它 `spawn` 真实二进制，这是「单元测试测函数、集成测试测接线」的分界线——main 里 detect → hint → launch 的**串联**只有跑起二进制才被覆盖。
- **`include_str!` + `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` 的 fixture 模式**：把 fixture 文件在编译期内嵌进测试二进制，路径用 `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/../<crate>/tests/<file>")` 跨 crate 引用。配合点是：fixture 有**唯一属主**（冻结 config 由 qwen4 crate 提交），消费方只引用、不复制——两份拷贝必然漂移。

再回顾两个贯穿全讲的旧结论：注册表构造期对 flag 的 id 与拼写做唯一性 panic（u2-l3）；`LaunchedEngine` 是迁移期 Handle/Stepped 二选一枚举，新线一律返回 `Stepped`（u3-l1）。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲关注点 |
|---|---|---|
| `../pegainfer-frontend/examples/echo-server.rs` | **官方参考实现**：无 GPU 完整模型线 | `EchoLine`、`EchoScheduler`、镜像的 main |
| `../pegainfer-frontend/examples/echo-model/config.json` | echo 线的「模型」fixture | `model_type: "echo"` 被 probe 认领 |
| `src/main.rs` | server 二进制：纯分发 | `model_lines()`、`families()`、hint 单测 |
| `Cargo.toml` | server 的依赖与 feature 表 | optional 依赖、feature 转发模式 |
| `tests/detect_gate.rs` | 检测门集成测试 | 双 fixture、两条出厂路径断言 |
| `../pegainfer-qwen4/src/model_line.rs` | detect_gate 的被测对象 | 「认领后诚实拒绝」的 launch |
| `../pegainfer-qwen4/src/probe.rs`（辅读） | qwen4 身份常量 | `MODEL_TYPE`/`TEXT_MODEL_TYPE` 绑定 |
| `../pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/driver.rs`（辅读） | Scheduler trait 与 drive 循环 | `spawn_scheduler` 的用法 |
| `../pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/wiring.rs`（辅读） | step 引擎交接包 | `Engine`/`EngineInfo` 字段语义 |
| `../Cargo.toml`（辅读） | workspace 成员表 | 新 crate 需在此登记 |

> 提醒：echo-server 与 detect_gate 全程不触达 CUDA；frontend crate 本身是 CUDA-free 的。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 EchoLine / EchoScheduler：一个不含 GPU 的完整模型线

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

接入新线前最自然的问题是：「我对 frontend 契约的**全部**义务到底是什么？」答案有两个极端：读 trait 定义（太抽象，看不到装配），或读 qwen3 的实现（太重，LoRA、P/D、显存预算全混在里面）。echo-server.rs 是刻意维护的中间态——**一条模型线的完整纵切面**：

```text
OpenAI HTTP (/v1/completions)
      │  vLLM 引擎协议（zmq + msgpack）
      ▼
SteppedEngineBridge（u4-l3）
      │  scheduler_pair 双端
      ▼
Scheduler contract：submit / step / metrics（u3-l5）
      │  RequestLedger 记账（u3-l4）
      ▼
EchoScheduler —— 引擎被换成「把 prompt 吐回去」的玩具
```

从 HTTP 到调度器契约的**每一层都是生产代码**，只有最底层的「模型」是假的。这使它同时充当三样东西：接入参考、frontend 契约的回归测试床（u3-l5、u4-l2 的实践都用它）、以及本仓库无 GPU 环境下的开发入口。

模型线本身（`EchoLine`）遵循「最小清单」：`probe` 认领一个 `config.json` 身份，`launch` 起调度器——没有独占 CLI flag，不消费任何非核心共享 flag。这正是 u2-l1 讲过的「三个必选方法 + 五个默认实现」的最小实例。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

echo-server 的 `main` 与 `pegainfer-server` 的 `main` 同构，只是把注册表缩减到一条线：

```text
ModelLineRegistry::new(vec![&MODEL_LINE])     # 只注册 echo 一条线
        │
        ▼ registry.build_command(clap::Command)   # 拼出含共享 flag 的 CLI
        ▼ 读 config.json → registry.detect        # probe 认领 model_type=="echo"
        ▼ validate_provided + shared.validate      # 与 server 完全相同
        ▼ LaunchContext → line.serve_plan          # 默认 ServePlan
        ▼ line.launch                              # 起 1 个 EchoScheduler
        ▼ vllm::serve_with_engine_count(...)       # 与 server 非 LoRA 分支同款
```

48	```text
49	OpenAI HTTP (/v1/completions)
50	      │  vLLM 引擎协议（zmq + msgpack）
51	      ▼
52	SteppedEngineBridge（u4-l3）
53	      │  scheduler_pair 双端

57	      ▼

61	从 HTTP 到调度器契约的**每一层都是生产代码**，只有最底层的「模型」是假的。这使它同时充当三样东西：接入参考、frontend 契约的回归测试床（u3-l5、u4-l2 的实践都用它）、以及本仓库无 GPU 环境下的开发入口。

# u5-l3 · 设计取舍复盘：纯分发二进制与契约迁移

## 1. 本讲目标

本讲是手册的收官篇，不再引入新的代码路径，而是把前四个单元走过的代码拉远，复盘支撑整个 `pegainfer-server` 的**三个架构决定**：

1. **server 只做纯分发**——一个约 300 行的二进制，不 import 任何模型 crate 的选项类型，新增模型线对 server 代码的改动只是注册表里的一行；
2. **`families()` 作为「必要的第二真相源」**——一份硬编码的身份表，为「被编译掉的模型线」补上检测提示，能力边界是 identity-only；
3. **两代引擎契约共存**——`LaunchedEngine` 枚举是带说明书的迁移脚手架，它写明了自己的删除条件。

学完本讲，你应该能：

- 论证纯分发二进制的收益清单与代价清单（收益不只是「少写代码」，还有编译期裁剪与错误语言的一致性；代价包括 `families()` 的重复与「trait 未表达的事 server 做不了」）；
- 界定 `feature_gate_hint` 的能力边界：它无法运行被编译掉的 probe，量化变体、绑词嵌入（tied embeddings）、YaRN 绳长外推这类「probe 会拒绝的变体」也会命中提示——提示只承诺身份归属，不承诺 checkpoint 可服务；
- 给出两代契约合并的判据：哪些模型线还压在 legacy 一侧、`KvPrefix` 为什么挡住删除、删除后 `main.rs` 与 `vllm/mod.rs` 里哪些分支会消失，以及 `ServePlan::default` 展开约定（CI 只编译三条线）为什么是契约演化的防漂移手段。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲建立在 u2-l3（注册表两本账）、u3-l1（两代契约地图）、u4-l1（serve 装配骨架）之上。在此之上补四个工程决策层面的概念：

- **真相源（source of truth）**：一份信息在仓库里被权威定义的位置。好的设计尽量只有一个真相源；当第二个真相源**不可避免**时（比如 `families()`），好的做法是承认它、写清它为什么必要、再用测试把两份真相**绑定**起来，让漂移（drift，两份拷贝各自演化后不再一致）在提交前被抓住。
- **identity-only（仅身份）**：检测分两层——**身份**（`model_type`、`architectures`，回答「这是哪个家族」）与**结构**（尺寸、量化、滑窗、RoPE 外推，回答「这个 checkpoint 我能不能服务」）。`families()` 表与多数 probe 只看身份；部分 probe（gemma4、kimi-k2）做结构校验。提示只建在身份层。
- **迁移脚手架（scaffolding）**：为平滑迁移而临时存在的结构。`LaunchedEngine` 枚举的文档注释里明确写着它将来会被删除——「会死的设计」也被当作设计的一部分来文档化，这是大型重构里非常值得学习的习惯。
- **编译可见性**：Rust 的 `#[cfg]` 让「代码没被编译」成为一等事实。CI 只编译部分 feature 组合时，**只有被编译的代码受编译器保护**；契约类型的演化（加字段、删变体）对未编译的 crate 是无声的。`ServePlan::default` 展开约定就是针对这一点的纪律。

再回顾三个贯穿本讲的旧结论：注册表构造期对 flag 的 id 与拼写做唯一性 panic（u2-l3）；`LaunchedEngine` 是迁移期 Handle/Stepped 二选一枚举，LoRA 分支只认 `Stepped`（u3-l1）；serve 函数族以「引擎 Future」为参数实现前端与引擎加载并发（u4-l1）。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲关注点 |
|---|---|---|
| `src/main.rs` | server 二进制：纯分发 | 模块文档、`model_lines()`、`families()`、`feature_gate_hint`、main 的三分支 |
| `Cargo.toml` | server 的依赖与 feature 表 | optional 依赖如何把「模型知识」挡在二进制之外 |
| `../pegainfer-frontend/src/model_line.rs` | 接缝：trait + 注册表 + SharedArgs | 模块文档的「No other server edits」、注册表自检、`ServePlan::default` 约定 |
| `../pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/mod.rs` | 引擎契约的两代分组地图 | 迁移边界的权威注释、扁平 re-export |
| `../pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/wiring.rs`（辅读） | `LaunchedEngine` 定义地 | 枚举文档的删除条件、两个 `From` 实现 |
| `../pegainfer-frontend/src/vllm/mod.rs`（辅读） | serve 装配骨架 | `engine_task` 对两变体各铸一桥的分派 |
| `../README.md` | 项目门面 | 架构边界表、「两代契约共存」的官方表述 |
| `../pegainfer-qwen3/src/config.rs`（辅读） | qwen3 的 probe | identity-only probe 的实例 |
| `../pegainfer-gemma4/src/probe.rs`、`../pegainfer-kimi-k2/src/config.rs`（辅读） | 结构校验型 probe | 「probe 会拒绝的变体」长什么样 |
| `../docs/subsystems/frontend/frontend-architecture.md`（辅读） | 前端架构文档 | 迁移顺序与删除清单的官方记录 |

> 提醒：本讲全部实践都是**源码阅读型与 grep 型**，不触达 CUDA，也不修改源码。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 server 纯分发设计：把「模型的多样性」关进 trait 对象

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

「纯分发（pure dispatch）」指 server 二进制对模型世界的全部知识 = 一列 `&'static dyn ModelLine` trait 对象。它做的事只有四件：**检测模型（detect）→ 校验 CLI（三级 validate）→ 启动引擎（launch）→ 分发服务（serve）**。任何模型特有的 flag、规则、选项类型都住在模型 crate 里，server 从不点名。

这样设计的收益：

- **新增模型线的改动面极小**：注册向量加一行 + `families()` 加一行 + 一个 Cargo feature。`main()` 本体、serve 装配、校验链一行不动。
- **编译期裁剪**：feature 未开启时整个模型 crate 不参与编译。出厂二进制（default = `qwen3`）里**物理上不存在**其他线的代码——这是 `#[cfg]` 给的免费瘦身，不需要任何运行时插件机制。
- **错误语言一致**：`launch` 失败是 `anyhow` 深层上下文链，server 只加一层上下文原样上抛（不分支、不翻译），于是所有模型线的启动错误对用户呈现同一种形态。
- **可测性**：注册表与 CLI 逻辑全部在 frontend crate，用 `StubLine` 就能测（u2-l3）；server 侧只需一个驱动真实二进制的 `detect_gate` 集成测试（u1-l4、u5-l2）。

代价同样真实，且后两个模块分别展开其中两条：

- **`families()` 重复**：被编译掉的线连 probe 都不在二进制里，身份表只能硬编码（→ 4.2）。
- **trait 表达力即 server 能力上限**：server 想在新阶段拿到新事实，就必须先在契约上加方法——`ServePlan` 正是这么长出来的（u2-l5）。
- **放弃穷尽匹配**：用 `dyn` trait 对象而不是枚举，意味着编译器不再强迫你「每加一条线就更新所有分派点」——注册表必须用**自建的两本账**（u2-l3）补回这份检查。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

先看依赖方向（frontend 架构文档的原话是 "thin bin"）：

```text
pegainfer-frontend  ←  pegainfer-core  ←  各模型 crate  ←  pegainfer-server（薄二进制）
     │                                                        │
     │ 定义：ModelLine trait、SharedArgs、LaunchedEngine、        │ 只持有
     │       ModelLineRegistry、serve 函数族                     │ &'static dyn ModelLine
     └──────────────── 契约类型全部由 frontend 拥有 ──────────────┘
```

main() 的装配线（u1-l3 详走过）在本讲视角下重读一遍——注意每一步都只经过 trait 或 frontend 类型：

```text
ModelLineRegistry::new(model_lines())     # 唯一「点名」模型 crate 的地方（cfg 守卫）
  → registry.build_command(...)            # 共享 flag + 各线独占 flag 合并
  → 读 config.json → registry.detect       # 经 probe 认领，拿到 &dyn ModelLine
  → validate_provided / shared.validate / line.validate   # 全部经 trait
  → line.serve_plan(&ctx)                  # 经 trait 拿服务形态
  → spawn_blocking(line.launch(&ctx))      # 经 trait 拿 LaunchedEngine
  → 按 plan 字段选 serve 分支               # 分派依据是 ServePlan，不是模型名！
```

关键观察：**main 的三个 serve 分支（LoRA / prefill-only / 默认）分派的依据是 `plan.lora_modules`、`plan.prefill_only`、`plan.scheduler_partition_count` 这三个「服务形态事实」，而不是「这是 Qwen3 还是 GLM」**。模型身份在 detect 之后就退役了，后续全部用抽象事实驱动——这就是纯分发能保持 300 行的原因。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**证据一：模块文档自我声明。** [src/main.rs:L1-L4](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-server/src/main.rs#L1-L4) 开宗明义："pure dispatch over the compiled-in `ModelLine`s. Every model-specific flag, rule, and option type lives in its model crate; this file only wires detection, CLI validation, and the serve path selection together."——这段注释就是本模块的「设计合同」。

**证据二：use 清单里没有任何模型 crate 的类型。** [src/main.rs:L6-L18](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-server/src/main.rs#L6-L18) 的全部导入是：`std::time::Instant`、`anyhow`、`clap::FromArgMatches`、`log`、`pegainfer_core::logging`、`pegainfer_frontend::engine::LaunchedEngine`、以及 `pegainfer_frontend::model_line` 下的六个契约项。**唯一出现的「模型知识」是 `SharedArgs`——而它定义在 frontend，不属于任何模型 crate**（这正是综合实践第 1 问的伏笔）。

**证据三：`model_lines()` 是模型 crate 被点名的唯一位置。** [src/main.rs:L24-L43](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-server/src/main.rs#L24-L43) 每行一个 `#[cfg(feature = ...)]` 守卫的 `&<crate>::model_line::MODEL_LINE`。feature 关掉，这一行连同 crate 一起从编译中消失。配合 [Cargo.toml:L34-L48](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-server/Cargo.toml#L34-L48) 的 feature 表（每个 feature = 一个 `optional` 依赖，见 [Cargo.toml:L18-L26](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-server/Cargo.toml#L18-L26)），「注册一行」与「编译一个 crate」被绑成同一个开关。

**证据四：接缝文档承诺「No other server edits」。** [../pegainfer-frontend/src/model_line.rs:L1-L12](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/a474b264537268022a9c06766f65c90ffd0be6c1/pegainfer-server/../pegainfer-frontend/src/model_line.rs#L1-L12) 写明接缝的设计意图："The server binary holds a feature-gated `ModelLineRegistry` and does pure dispatch — it never names a model crate's option types.
